claim: Ratchet violations are read from the merged output: run_child returns stdout then stderr in one string, so a warning on stderr becomes a new violation on every run.
The baseline is read from the check copy after the command ran; a guard that rewrites its own baseline (rubocop --auto-gen-config, tee) passes every violation.
Output cut at MAX_OUTPUT (16 MiB) or by the 2 s pipe drain makes missing lines look fixed, and tightening deletes real baseline lines.
Path::components drops inner `.` and empty components, so `a/./b` and `a//b` would load although AC-1 and AC-2 refuse `.`; the check must split the string at `/`.
Committing a tightened baseline moves HEAD past the passing check record; no criterion says whether the close needs another full check, and the AC-10 line does not ask for the commit.
Guards rely on the lazy checkout of Runner::project; with no project commands, or after a project command that edits files, guards may run in a stale or dirty copy.
A dir such as tests or src passes the lexical check, so every builder write under it is denied and every main-agent edit asks; refuse or warn about a dir that overlaps source or test folders.
The record test of step 3 has only exit-code guards; nonzero new and removed counts of ratchet guards are tested nowhere.

LOW list: the case-insensitive compare differs from the inode check of toml_edit_ask; the precedence of a missing baseline against a broken exit code; whether n counts distinct lines; the guard name is not printed through printable; a non-UTF-8 or unreadable baseline; names that differ by whitespace; step 7 asks in bypass mode until step 8; no record field for a tightening.

note: RunResult gains stdout apart from the merged output; violations come from stdout only, the tail of AC-3 and AC-9 from both; a stderr line beside known violations is a case of known_violations_pass
the baseline is read from the HEAD commit (git object) before the command runs; a command that overwrites its baseline in the copy is a case of a_new_violation_fails

when stdout reached MAX_OUTPUT or the drain deadline the guard is unverified: output cut, and nothing is written; a command that hides its own failure and prints nothing goes to Not promised; a case in fixed_violations_leave_the_baseline
dir and baseline are checked as strings split at `/`: empty, `.` or `..` components, a backslash or NUL refuse, one trailing `/` of dir is allowed; `a//b` and `a/./b` cases for both

new AC-15 and step 10: a passing check record stays valid for the close after commits that change only baseline files of ratchet guards, each new file's lines a subset of the old; the AC-10 line ends with `; commit it`
before the first guard the copy is checked out at HEAD with tracked changes discarded; cases with no project commands and with a project command that edits a tracked file
outside the promise: listed in the Summary for the person to decide at the close
the record counts of ratchet guards are asserted in known_violations_pass, a_new_violation_fails and fixed_violations_leave_the_baseline, which AC-11 names

AC-3 prints the name through printable; AC-9 comes before AC-8; n counts distinct lines; the baseline is read lossy as UTF-8 from git; the case-insensitive compare stays because it can only ask more (agent decision); the rest no change
